column3: NASB puts “that is, Gideon” in parentheses; “the spring of Harod” renders “En-harod.”
“become boastful” renders “glorify itself”; “My own power” renders “my hand.”
“the 300 men took the people’s provisions” interprets a difficult Hebrew clause; NASB supplies “Gideon.”
“the same night” renders “that night”; “hands” renders the Hebrew singular “hand.”
“outposts” renders “edge of those arrayed for battle.”
“a loaf” renders “a round loaf”; “lay flat” renders “fell.”
“Look at me” renders “From me you will see”; “outskirts” renders “edge.”
“when they had just posted the watch” renders the doubled verb.
NASB supplies “when” and reads “one against another” for “each against his neighbor.”
“the men of Israel” renders the collective “the man of Israel.”
“take the waters before them” renders “capture the waters for them.”
